newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba - longer M3 period takes account of EMU.
newsitem.headline: Buba - longer M3 period takes account of EMU.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday it was extending its money supply orientation to a two-year period to take into account the environment for German monetary policy in the run-up to European monetary union.

The extension to a two-year period from the traditional one-year period was also intended to limit possible uncertainty about monetary policy ahead of monetary union, the Bundesbank said in a statement.
The Bundesbank also said that it was maintaining the target corridor at three percent for 1997 to take into account the continuing short-term volatility of money supply developments.
But it added that the long-term link between money supply developments and inflation remained intact.
The Bundesbank set a target of 3.5 to 6.5 percent for 1997, compared with four to seven percent for 1996, and said it regarded M3 growth of about five percent as appropriate for 1997 and 1998.
